# 1.2.43 - the audit round, and the module speaks Polish

The module speaks Polish, and the whole of it was read again with the audit's
eyes: a GM and three players through a Daily Life time of day, a murder, a case,
a trial and the turn of a chapter, on a four-client harness, with every domain of
the code reviewed against what the interface actually said to whom. This is the
audit's round; the copy itself is being reworded by hand and comes as 1.3.0.

**Language.** A new *Language* setting, English or Polski, at the top of the Look
dialog behind the gear in the corner, and in the module's settings. It is the
module's own setting, per browser, English by default, and separate from
Foundry's core language on purpose: most of these tables play on an English
Foundry, and the layer they want in Polish is this one - the sheet, the panel,
the HUD, the cards, the dialogs - not the whole client. Every sentence the module
owns is translated, including the ones `config.mjs` carries inline (action hints,
Call effects, item categories, the trial's instructions), which are swapped in
place at load so no reader of the rulebook has to know a translation exists.
Counted sentences carry the four Polish plural forms. The glossary stays English
in every language, as the game's proper names: Hope, Despair, Sanity, Truth
Bullets, Remnants, Blackened, Class Trial, Daily Life, Eclipse, the Calls, the
actions, the statistics. Changing the language asks for a reload, the same way
Foundry's own does. The pixel face, VT323 and Special Elite all ship a Latin
Extended file, so ą, ę, ł, ś, ż render in the same typeface as the rest of the
word.

**The Class Trial and the chapter, from the panel.** The most repeated gesture in
a session - advancing the time of day and refilling actions - is now one button
on the panel's clock line, refused during an Eclipse with a reason. The panel's
"next" line points at the Eclipse when every student has acted, and at the End
of chapter screen once the verdict is in; that screen is also a tile under
*Between sessions*, and its button no longer waits for the verdict, since it is
also how a chapter ends without a trial.

**What the audit corrected.** The remnant ledger's socket answered anyone who
asked for it, GM or not, and could answer itself; it now checks the sender and
replies to them alone. A player who was the incident's third could see the
killer's trace through the fog if they had sided with the victim; the trace is
now shown to the killer's side only, and the opening card seats the same set of
participants the murder does. A Despair Call that needed the GM was charged its
cooldown before the GM ruled; it is charged when the GM says yes. The Breakdown
and Wounded sounds were looked up under the wrong keys and never played. Worn
items lost their worn state when they were moved between owners; a stowed item
kept reading as equipped. Palm could not be rerolled. The day's summary named the
time of day by its key. A Direct Murder with no GM online spent the action and
parked nothing; it now refuses first. A hint request charged the action's cost
twice. Season reset forgot the called assembly and the killing-game rules, and
each student's rests and betrayal window. The investigation's Save wrote rows
that were not on the form. The vote's floor did not refresh when a ballot came
in, and a player's client tried to run the GM's reminder. Every request to the
GM is now sent to the GMs alone rather than to the whole table, and the messenger
sound reached the GM only for other people's messages. The safeword card named
the socket's sender rather than what the payload claimed. The curtain left its
size limits behind on unmount, missed a resize while one was pending, and could
place a click on the wrong pane. The fog's ledger was keyed to one scene, faded
an outline it had not drawn, and did not free what it destroyed. The Mastermind
saw rooms as unentered. The spend card said the wrong pool. The armed-Call
whisper said "by nobody" to the person who armed it. The reduced-motion switch
hid under the Legacy theme.

**Text.** Some thirty strings reworded: a count where a placeholder said "{n}", a note
that promised a sweep the module does itself, a phase explanation that described
the previous release's behaviour, and a set of GM-only sentences that were
reaching players through the cards.

**Hygiene.** The harness runs four clients (a GM and three players); two new
scenarios walk a Daily Life time of day and the language switch. The suite gained
a check that `lang/pl.json` covers every English key and every placeholder, and
the release workflow now refuses a tag whose stylesheet stamp does not match the
manifest - the 1.2.42 stylesheet still said 1.2.41.

Suite: 116 passed on the harness (the 13 that fail there need a real canvas and
a real stylesheet, and pass in Foundry).

## Known, and deliberately left

The audit's full report and its task list are in `audit/AUDIT-1.2.42.md`, with
the method and the pitfalls of each item. The larger ones - the messenger's
threads being readable by any player who asks the world for them, the trap and
GM-only cards that render dead buttons for players, the whisper metadata that
names the incident's participants to a player who inspects a message - are
design changes rather than corrections and are queued there rather than rushed
into this release.
